dedupe_keys.name: global covid 19 lockdown hourly electricity demand profiles

description: Fortunatus, Haas and Peer release cross-country hourly electricity-demand profiles linked to COVID-19 lockdown phases. The public Zenodo record is CC BY 4.0 and includes demand CSVs, seasonal and day-type tables, lockdown-period data, Python and SQL processing files. Its own description says 35 countries are represented and typical hours are segmented by season and weekday or weekend. A power-system modeller can use these patterns to test demand shocks or capacity planning with model-pypsa after aligning geography and time zones. A caveat is that the strictest lockdown period is defined from policy-stringency scores, while actual load change also reflects weather, industrial mix and behaviour. The published medoid-style typical profiles should not replace the full raw hourly sequence for event timing. National source periods vary, and upstream IEA or operator data may have different reuse terms. I read the own Zenodo metadata and article availability statement without downloading files, rerunning scripts or attributing load changes causally to policy.
